title.narrative: Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance Core Contributions for Financial Years 2021-22 to 2025-26

description.narrative: Core funding contributions to Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance for financial years 2021-22 to 2025-26. This investment totals AUD300 million, and will deliver access to new and underused vaccines globally - including in the Indo-Pacific. The funding is pooled with other donor core-contributions. Its utilisation is overseen by the Gavi Board on which Australia is represented.

title.narrative: Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance Core Contributions for Financial Years 2021-22 to 2025-26

description.narrative: Australia, through our support for Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, supported low and middle-income countries to help strengthen their health systems, especially at the primary healthcare level, which in turn supported these countries to improve routine vaccination coverage and introduce new vaccines. Gavi provided cash grants to both ministries of health and partner organisations to build health care workers’ capacity, develop better health information systems, strengthen networks of community health workers, improve strategic planning, program management and health financing, increase vaccine-preventable disease surveillance, and improve supply chain management. For example, in the Solomon Islands, the Ministry of Health used a portion of Gavi’s Health Systems Strengthening grant together with technical assistance provided through WHO to strengthen their health information systems. Similarly, with UNICEF technical assistance, Gavi’s funds were used to strengthen the country’s vaccine supply chain and procure cold chain equipment including solar fridges installed in community health centres.

In 2022 Australia, through Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, supported 16 new vaccine introductions (against a target of 15) including 6 Measles and 5 HPV introductions. Gavi also helped countries provide routine immunisations to more than 68 million children, reducing the number of children who had not received any vaccination from 12.4 million in 2021 to 10.2 million in 2022. DTP3 vaccine coverage in countries supported by Gavi increased by 3%, and HPV vaccine coverage increased to 10%. Preventative measles vaccination campaigns resulted in 70.2% of children aged under five receiving at least one dose, an increase from 37.3% in 2021. Gavi’s efforts helped increase the number of global manufacturers supplying prequalified vaccines from five in 2001 to 19 in 2022, with more than 50 percent based in low and middle-income countries and resulting in lower price points. (Most recent Gavi data reported; 2023 data will be reported in 2025.)
